findings.title: website_name bypasses the untrusted-attribute filter and leaks TL0 users' website
findings.body: `website` is in `untrusted_attributes` (line 109), so it is hidden from anonymous viewers when `scope.restrict_user_fields?` is true (TL0 users). The new `website_name` attribute is not added to `untrusted_attributes`, and the manual guard `include_website_name` (without `?`) is never executed by the serializer, so anonymous visitors still receive `website_name`. Because `website_name` contains the host and, when it matches the instance domain, the full path, this re-exposes the exact URL that the untrusted restriction is meant to hide. Add `:website_name` to `untrusted_attributes` (which will also define the correct `include_website_name?` predicate) and update the untrusted-attributes spec.

findings.title: include_website_name is missing the `?` suffix and is never called
findings.body: ActiveModel::Serializers decides whether to emit an attribute by calling `include_<attr>?`; every other predicate in this file (e.g. `include_email?`, `include_stats?`, `include_suspend_reason?`) uses the question mark. Because this method is defined as `include_website_name` without `?`, it is dead code: `website_name` is always serialized, including `website_name: null` for users with no website, and any conditional exclusion written here would silently do nothing. Rename it to `include_website_name?`.

findings.title: Domain comparison is asymmetric and can treat unrelated domains as equal
findings.body: The path is appended only when the instance host ends with '.'+website_host (else branch) or when both hosts have the same label count > 2 and their labels after the first match (elsif). As a result, instance `example.com` with website `www.example.com` (2 vs 3 labels) falls into the else branch, fails `ends_with?('.www.example.com')`, and returns only `www.example.com`, while the reverse case (`forum.example.com` instance, `example.com` website) shows the path. The feature therefore works inconsistently. In addition, comparing all-but-the-first labels treats unrelated registrable domains under multi-label public suffixes as identical: `foo.co.uk` and `bar.co.uk` both reduce to `co.uk`, so the full path of one is shown as if it belonged to the other. Use a proper registrable-domain/subdomain comparison instead of label counting.

findings.title: New specs miss the untrusted/anonymous leak and the elsif branch
findings.body: The added examples only cover different domains and the equal/parent-domain cases. There is no example for a TL0 user with a website viewed by an anonymous guardian, so the `website_name` privacy leak is not caught, and the `untrusted_attributes` list at line 11 still omits `website_name`. The `elsif` branch (same label count, different subdomain, e.g. `www.example.com` vs `forum.example.com`) that the code comment describes is never exercised, nor is a user with a blank website (the `include_website_name` behavior). Add these cases so the serializer's inclusion and matching logic is verified.
